sections.title: Basic Definition & Eccentricity
sections.content: A conic is the locus of a point whose distance from a fixed point (Focus) and a fixed line (Directrix) is in a constant ratio called eccentricity (e). If e = 1, it's a Parabola. If e < 1, it's an Ellipse. If e > 1, it's a Hyperbola.

sections.title: Standard Parabola
sections.content: Equation: y² = 4ax. Vertex: (0,0). Focus: (a,0). Directrix: x = -a. Axis: y = 0 (X-axis). Latus Rectum length = 4a. Other forms are y² = -4ax, x² = 4ay, and x² = -4ay.

sections.title: Standard Ellipse
sections.content: Equation: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (Assume a > b). Center: (0,0). Foci: (±ae, 0). Directrices: x = ±a/e. Major axis length = 2a, Minor axis length = 2b. Eccentricity formula: b² = a²(1 - e²).

sections.title: Standard Hyperbola
sections.content: Equation: x²/a² - y²/b² = 1. Center: (0,0). Foci: (±ae, 0). Directrices: x = ±a/e. Transverse axis = 2a, Conjugate axis = 2b. Eccentricity formula: b² = a²(e² - 1).

sections.title: Latus Rectum and Focal Distance
sections.content: Latus Rectum (LR) is the focal chord perpendicular to the axis. Length for Parabola = 4a. Length for Ellipse and Hyperbola = 2b²/a. Focal distance is the distance of a point (x,y) on the conic from its focus.

sections.title: Parametric Coordinates
sections.content: Parabola (y²=4ax): (at², 2at). Ellipse: (a cosθ, b sinθ). Hyperbola: (a secθ, b tanθ). These are used to represent any general point on the curve using a single variable.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Confusing a > b and a < b cases in the ellipse, which changes the foci to the Y-axis.
2) Forgetting that eccentricity e > 1 for a hyperbola, leading to sign errors in b² = a²(e²-1).
3) Misidentifying the directrix equation of x² = 4ay (it is y = -a, not x = -a).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 covers identifying the conic shape from 'e', memorizing the standard equations, foci, directrices, and lengths of axes/latus rectum, and knowing their parametric forms.

tricks.title: Identify Conic from General Equation
tricks.explanation: For ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, first ensure Δ ≠ 0. If h² = ab (Parabola). If h² < ab (Ellipse). If h² > ab (Hyperbola). If a+b=0 along with h²>ab (Rectangular Hyperbola).
tricks.example: x² + 4xy + y² = 0. h=2, a=1, b=1. h² (4) > ab (1). It's a Hyperbola.

tricks.title: Quick Ellipse Eccentricity
tricks.explanation: Use e = √[1 - (Minor Axis)² / (Major Axis)²]. Just divide the smaller denominator by the larger one.

tricks.title: Quick Hyperbola Eccentricity
tricks.explanation: Use e = √[1 + (Conjugate Axis)² / (Transverse Axis)²]. Just divide the negative term's denominator by the positive term's denominator.

tricks.title: Focal Distance Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Parabola: distance = |x + a|. Ellipse: distance from foci are (a - ex) and (a + ex). Sum of focal distances is ALWAYS 2a.
tricks.example: Point (x,y) on ellipse x²/25+y²/9=1. Sum of distances from both foci is 2(5) = 10.

tricks.title: Finding Center by Partial Differentiation
tricks.explanation: To find the center of any general 2nd-degree conic (ellipse/hyperbola), partially differentiate the equation with respect to x (treating y as constant) and then y. Set both to 0 and solve the linear equations.

tricks.title: Quick Latus Rectum
tricks.explanation: If the equation is in standard form, Latus Rectum of Ellipse/Hyperbola = 2 * (Minor/Conjugate)² / (Major/Transverse).
